summary: Tzolk'in has players place workers onto interlocking gears that physically rotate each round, so a worker placed on a low-value early spot slowly moves toward more powerful actions the longer it's left in place — but you have to pay corn upkeep to leave workers out and pull them at the wrong moment forfeits the better reward. The result is a worker-placement game with a distinctive timing puzzle layered on top of standard resource and building management.
praised: the rotating gear mechanism is genuinely innovative and tactile
strong risk/reward tension in deciding when to pull workers
criticised: punishing for new players who mistime the gears
corn upkeep can create a snowballing problem for players who fall behind
fiddly component overhead (gears, resources, temple tracks)
can run long for the amount of choice on a given turn

interaction.kind: worker placement blocking on shared rotating gears
interaction.detail: All players place workers on the same set of gears, so popular spots get blocked or bumped, forcing rivals onto worse options, while resource and building tracks are otherwise managed on each player's own board. The temple tracks and available action spots are the main shared state.

scoring.how_you_win: You place and later retrieve workers on rotating gears to climb temple tracks and construct buildings/monuments; after the fixed 26 turns (13 in shorter games), converted resources and accumulated VP are summed and the highest total wins.
